h1: Milvus vs Vespa: an open-source vector database comparison
intro: Milvus vs Vespa is a comparison of two different kinds of system: Milvus is a vector database built on storage-compute separation, while Vespa, open-sourced by Yahoo, is a full search and serving engine whose content nodes keep data, indexes and ranking on local disk and memory. Milvus adds a stateless node and loads segments from object storage; Vespa adds a content node and redistributes buckets, which its docs say can take hours. Choose Milvus for elastic billion-scale vector search with simple operations; choose Vespa when multi-phase ranking with ML models in the serving path is the core of the product.

sections.h2: Milvus vs Vespa scalability: how does each grow to billions of vectors?
paragraphs: Milvus is built on storage-compute separation. Segments and the write-ahead log live in object storage, so a new query node loads its assigned segments instead of copying another node's disk, and ingestion, search and indexing scale on separate node types. Tiered storage lets a query node serve datasets larger than its memory and disk by pulling field data on demand.

Vespa scalability follows the classic search-engine model: stateless container clusters handle queries, stateful content clusters store data and indexes, and a config-server cluster backed by ZooKeeper, typically three nodes, holds the deployment. Each content node runs proton, which keeps the document store on local disk and attributes and HNSW graphs in memory. Adding a content node triggers automatic bucket redistribution; Vespa's docs note this can take hours and raises load on the node meanwhile.

sections.h2: Milvus vs Vespa performance: which is faster?
paragraphs: VectorDBBench, the open-source benchmark behind the public leaderboard, has a Vespa client, but no Vespa result is published on the leaderboard, so this page shows only the Milvus and Zilliz Cloud rows. Vespa's blog cites a Marqo internal benchmark at 50 million vectors without hardware, index, version or method, so it is not charted. For a Milvus vs Vespa performance number on your own data, run VectorDBBench against both on the same dataset and hardware.

sections.h2: Vespa vs Milvus features: a vector database comparison table
paragraphs: Vespa is a search engine first: one HNSW implementation plus exact search, a deep ranking stack and a tensor framework that holds many vectors per document. Milvus is a vector database first: many index families, server-side BM25 for hybrid search, StructArray fields for ColBERT late interaction, and rerank functions that run inside the database.

sections.h2: Milvus vs Vespa cost and operations: what does each take to run?
paragraphs: Cost in both systems is memory on the nodes that serve the index, plus, in Vespa, the CPU that evaluates rank profiles and ONNX models at query time. Milvus trims memory with quantized HNSW, DiskANN and tiered storage; Vespa sizes content nodes for attributes and HNSW graphs in RAM. Neither needs Kubernetes to start.

sections.h2: When is Vespa the better choice?
paragraphs: Vespa is a mature engine with a ranking stack few systems match. Teams looking for Vespa alternatives usually want elastic scaling and simpler operations; if ranking logic is the product, Vespa's design is an advantage.
bullets: Relevance needs multi-phase ranking with learned models (ONNX, XGBoost) evaluated on the serving path.
The application is text-heavy search with structured fields, grouping and rank expressions in one schema.
Your team already runs Vespa and knows application packages, services.xml and content clusters.
You want personal-index search over many small user corpora via streaming mode.
You prefer Vespa Cloud and its managed deployment pipeline for the whole search application.

faqs: Which is faster, Milvus or Vespa?

No published VectorDBBench result exists for Vespa. On Cohere 1M, Milvus-16c64g-sq4u-fp16-force_merge lists 9,575.69 QPS at P99 2.3 ms and ZillizCloud-8cu-perf 13,316.23 QPS at P99 2 ms. VectorDBBench ships a Vespa client for the same test.

Vespa describes itself as a serving engine that stores, computes and ranks big data at serving time, with vector search via HNSW and exact nearestNeighbor. Milvus is a purpose-built vector database with storage-compute separation.

Both are search engines with text, structured and vector retrieval on local-disk shards; Vespa adds phased ranking with ONNX models. Milvus is the vector-first alternative to either: object-storage segments, more index types and server-side BM25. See Milvus vs Elasticsearch.
Can Vespa be used for RAG?

Yes. Vespa offers LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations and in-engine embedders, including ColBERT and SPLADE. Milvus integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack and Dify, and fuses server-side BM25 sparse vectors with dense results for RAG retrieval.
Can Vespa scale to billions of vectors?

Vespa scales by adding content nodes, with buckets redistributed automatically, which its docs say can take hours; tensor fields and HNSW graphs are in-memory per content node. Milvus Distributed is documented for tens of billions of vectors on object storage.
Does Milvus support multiple vectors per document like Vespa?

Yes. A collection holds up to 10 vector fields by default, and StructArray fields store a list of vectors per entity that EmbeddingList search scores with MAX_SIM for ColBERT and ColPali. Vespa stores the same thing as a mixed tensor matched by its closest vector.
Is Milvus easier to operate than Vespa?

Milvus Lite runs inside pymilvus, Standalone is one Docker image for up to about 100 million vectors, and Distributed runs on Kubernetes. Self-managed Vespa needs a config-server quorum, container and content clusters, and an application package for every schema change.

Yes. Vespa and Milvus are both Apache-2.0 and self-hostable; Vespa was open-sourced by Yahoo in 2017, Milvus is an LF AI & Data graduated project. Each has a managed service: Vespa Cloud, and Zilliz Cloud, the fully managed Milvus with the same client API.
